summary: The note covers the rise of collaborative interdisciplinary student projects, as presented at the Local Education Systems conference on September 5, 2023. It describes how such projects work through collaboration, synergy, a phased structure, soft-skill development, reflective assessment, and technology, with example projects from fall 2023. The note ends with an empty section on educator development.
one_line: Overview of how collaborative interdisciplinary student projects are structured, assessed, and supported by technology, drawn from the September 2023 Local Education Systems conference.
key_facts: The Local Education Systems conference took place on September 5, 2023, shortly after the start of the new school year.
Sarah White, a curriculum developer, and James Hartley, a thought leader in innovative pedagogy, shared insights at the conference.

James Hartley said in his keynote: "Effective collaboration requires clear communication, an understanding of each discipline's workflows, and a mutual respect for the unique value each student brings to the table."
An example scenario has high school programmers, artists, scientists, and writers building a video game that teaches players about environmental issues.

A classroom ran an urban planning project from October 10 to November 21, 2023, in which students presented a model city balancing economic growth with ecological sustainability; it reflects the STEAM approach.
Sarah White recommends a phased approach: identify a central challenge, then research, ideation, prototyping, and final presentation, with check-ins and reflections at each phase.
Sarah White presented a case study completed on December 15, 2023, in which students designed a community garden that doubled as an outdoor learning environment for a local primary school.

An after-school program from September 25 to October 30, 2023, had students create a multimedia marketing campaign promoting energy conservation, building communication, leadership, time management, and critical thinking.
A water conservation campaign project ran from November 3 to December 22, 2023, and used a rubric with individual reflective journals plus feedback from community stakeholders.
Assessment frameworks discussed emphasize peer evaluations, process journals, and reflective essays alongside traditional products like models or presentations.
Tools cited for collaboration and organization include Google Workspace, Trello, and Asana, and digital portfolios show student progress over time.

Daniel Gomez, a software engineer in educational technology, developed a project-based learning platform launched on October 1, 2023, presented at the conference as a one-stop-shop for managing interdisciplinary projects.
